name: Pseudo-Cleft
pattern: Clause[Subject:NP[fused relative] + be + PredComp:XP[value]], or reversed alignment

entry.name: Pseudo-Cleft
entry.pattern: Clause[Subject:NP[fused relative] + be + PredComp:XP[value]], or reversed alignment

1.definition: Specifies the value of a variable defined by a fused relative.
1.details: The fused relative in What I need is a long cool drink defines what is to be identified. The value can precede be in the reversed version. Clausal values are common, including a bare or to-infinitival when the relative has do. A copular clause that evaluates what they did as a disgrace is ascriptive and does not specify the action.

examples.form: [What I need is a long cool drink.]
examples.note: The drink supplies the value of what I need.

examples.form: [A long cool drink is what I need.]
[What you must do is apply for special leave.]
examples.note: Bare infinitival value. To is also possible here.

grounds.note: Lists multiple phrase and clause types in the post-be position.

projection.target: A do pseudo-cleft can take an infinitival value which the corresponding it-cleft generally excludes.
projection.evidence: CGEL compares the two clefts with matched clausal values and distinguishes specifying and ascriptive be. CASA catalogs the wh-cleft pattern.

curious.title: What I need is...
curious.summary: A sentence can start with a what clause, then a form of be, and finish with the thing being named.
curious.body: In What I need is a long cool drink, the first part sets up a gap: what is it that I need? The last part fills it in: a long cool drink. Putting the answer last gives it emphasis. The order can be flipped, as in A long cool drink is what I need. The answer can also be an action, as in What you must do is apply for special leave. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.

examples.text: [What I need is a long cool drink.]
[A long cool drink is what I need.]
[What you must do is apply for special leave.]

curious.try: Start with what I want is, and finish with the thing you want. Then flip it around.

teacher.summary: Covers sentences like What I need is a drink, where a what clause is paired with the value that completes it.
teacher.explain: A pseudo-cleft specifies the value of a variable defined by a fused relative. In What I need is a long cool drink, what I need defines what is to be identified, and the drink supplies the value. The value can precede be in the reversed version (A long cool drink is what I need). Clausal values are common, including a bare or to-infinitival when the relative has do (What you must do is apply for special leave; to is also possible). This dictionary says the do pseudo-cleft can take an infinitival value which the corresponding it-cleft generally excludes. It's marked provisional.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called a wh-cleft; the part beginning with what is a fused relative in this dictionary's terms.

examples.text: [What I need is a long cool drink.]
[A long cool drink is what I need.]
[What you must do is apply for special leave.]

contrasts.text: What they did was a disgrace.
contrasts.note: A copular clause that evaluates what they did, not one that specifies the action.

watch_for: A learner might treat What they did was a disgrace as a pseudo-cleft, when it evaluates the action instead of naming it.
A learner might leave out the be that links the two parts.
teacher.activity: Students turn plain sentences such as I need a long cool drink into pseudo-clefts and then into the reversed version, and say which part is the value.
